title: “The Mousetrap” opens
text: In November 1952, Agatha Christie’s play “The Mousetrap” opened in London’s West End. It became the longest-running play in the world, and audiences are still asked to keep the ending a secret.

title: ITV and the first adverts
text: On September 22, 1955, ITV went on air and Britain saw its first television advert, for Gibbs SR toothpaste. Suddenly there was a second channel to choose.

title: Lonnie Donegan: “Rock Island Line”
text: In 1956 Lonnie Donegan’s “Rock Island Line” started the skiffle craze. Thousands of teenagers formed groups with a cheap guitar, a washboard and a tea-chest bass.

title: Cliff Richard: “Move It”
text: In 1958 a 17-year-old Cliff Richard released “Move It”, often called the first real British rock and roll record.

title: The Shadows: “Apache”
text: In the summer of 1960, The Shadows went to number one with the instrumental “Apache”. Hank Marvin’s echoing guitar made countless boys want a red Stratocaster.

title: The Big Freeze
text: The winter of 1962–63 was one of the coldest on record. Snow lay for more than two months, rivers and even the sea froze in places, and football fixtures were postponed for weeks.
wiki: Winter of 1962–63 in the United Kingdom

title: The Beatles: “She Loves You”
text: In August 1963 The Beatles released “She Loves You”. “Yeah, yeah, yeah” was heard everywhere, and it became the best-selling single of the decade in Britain.

title: Cilla Black: “Anyone Who Had a Heart”
text: In February 1964, Cilla Black from Liverpool reached number one with “Anyone Who Had a Heart”. She had been a cloakroom girl at the Cavern Club.
listen: Cilla Black Anyone Who Had a Heart

title: The Kinks: “You Really Got Me”
text: In 1964 The Kinks hit number one with “You Really Got Me”, built on a rough, loud guitar riff that nobody had heard the like of before.
listen: The Kinks You Really Got Me

title: Churchill’s funeral
text: On January 30, 1965, Sir Winston Churchill was given a state funeral. Thousands lined the streets of London, and the cranes along the Thames dipped as his coffin passed by boat.
wiki: Death and state funeral of Winston Churchill

title: Tom Jones: “It’s Not Unusual”
text: In March 1965, Tom Jones from Pontypridd reached number one with “It’s Not Unusual”. It was the start of a career that lasted more than half a century.

title: The Rolling Stones: “Satisfaction”
text: In 1965 The Rolling Stones released “(I Can’t Get No) Satisfaction”. Keith Richards said the famous riff came to him in his sleep.

title: Dusty Springfield: “You Don’t Have to Say You Love Me”
text: In 1966 Dusty Springfield reached number one with “You Don’t Have to Say You Love Me”, her biggest hit.
wiki: You Don't Have to Say You Love Me
listen: Dusty Springfield You Don't Have to Say You Love Me

title: Procol Harum: “A Whiter Shade of Pale”
text: In the summer of 1967, “A Whiter Shade of Pale” by Procol Harum, with its slow organ tune, spent six weeks at number one.
listen: Procol Harum A Whiter Shade of Pale

title: “Sgt. Pepper”
text: In 1967 The Beatles released “Sgt. Pepper’s Lonely Hearts Club Band”. People studied the crowded cover for hours while the record played.
wiki: Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band
listen: The Beatles With a Little Help from My Friends

title: Sandie Shaw wins Eurovision
text: In 1967 Sandie Shaw, singing barefoot as always, won the Eurovision Song Contest for the United Kingdom with “Puppet on a String”.
listen: Sandie Shaw Puppet on a String

title: Mary Hopkin: “Those Were the Days”
text: In 1968, 18-year-old Mary Hopkin from Wales reached number one with “Those Were the Days”, produced by Paul McCartney.
listen: Mary Hopkin Those Were the Days

title: “Dad’s Army”
text: In 1968 “Dad’s Army” began on BBC One. Captain Mainwaring and the Home Guard of Walmington-on-Sea are still being repeated today.

title: “Monty Python’s Flying Circus”
text: In October 1969 “Monty Python’s Flying Circus” first appeared on the BBC, late on a Sunday night. Comedy was never quite the same again.

title: Slade: “Merry Xmas Everybody”
text: At Christmas 1973, Slade were number one with “Merry Xmas Everybody”. It has been played every December since.

title: ABBA win in Brighton
text: On April 6, 1974, ABBA won the Eurovision Song Contest in Brighton with “Waterloo”.

title: “Fawlty Towers”
text: In 1975 John Cleese checked in as Basil Fawlty, the rudest hotel owner in Torquay. Only twelve episodes of “Fawlty Towers” were ever made.

title: Queen: “Bohemian Rhapsody”
text: At the end of 1975, Queen’s “Bohemian Rhapsody” spent nine weeks at number one. It was almost six minutes long, and radio played it anyway.

title: The long hot summer of 1976
text: In the summer of 1976, Britain baked for weeks. Reservoirs dried up, standpipes appeared in some streets, and a Minister for Drought was appointed — just before the rain came.

title: Virginia Wade wins Wimbledon
text: On July 1, 1977, in the Queen’s Silver Jubilee year and with the Queen watching, Virginia Wade won the women’s singles at Wimbledon.

title: Botham’s Ashes
text: In the summer of 1981, Ian Botham turned the Ashes around almost on his own. At Headingley, England won after being made to follow on.

title: Torvill and Dean’s “Boléro”
text: On February 14, 1984, Jayne Torvill and Christopher Dean skated to Ravel’s “Boléro” at the Sarajevo Olympics and won gold with a row of perfect sixes.

title: “EastEnders”
text: On February 19, 1985, the BBC opened the doors of the Queen Vic. “EastEnders” and Albert Square were soon watched by millions.

title: “The Tin Drum”
text: In 1959 Günter Grass published “The Tin Drum”, the story of Oskar, the boy who refused to grow. It made him famous around the world.

title: The Beatles in Hamburg
text: In August 1960 an unknown group from Liverpool began playing night after night in the clubs of Hamburg’s St. Pauli. The Beatles learned their trade there.

title: Conny Froboess: “Zwei kleine Italiener”
text: In 1962 Conny Froboess sang “Zwei kleine Italiener”, about two homesick guest workers. It was one of the biggest hits of the year.

title: Drafi Deutscher: “Marmor, Stein und Eisen bricht”
text: In 1965 Drafi Deutscher sang “Marmor, Stein und Eisen bricht” — “but our love will not”. Everyone could sing along with the “dam-dam”.
listen: Drafi Deutscher Marmor Stein und Eisen bricht

title: “Beat-Club”
text: In September 1965 Radio Bremen began “Beat-Club”, the first German television show for young people’s music. Parents were warned beforehand.

title: The “ZDF-Hitparade”
text: In January 1969 Dieter Thomas Heck began presenting the “ZDF-Hitparade”, speaking faster than anyone else on television. Schlager fans did not miss it.

title: “Dalli Dalli”
text: From 1971 Hans Rosenthal presented the quiz show “Dalli Dalli”. When the audience liked a round, he jumped in the air and called “Das war Spitze!”

title: “Sesamstraße”
text: In January 1973 “Sesame Street” came to German television. Ernie, Bert and the Cookie Monster soon spoke German.

title: The car-free Sundays
text: On November 25, 1973, during the oil crisis, driving was banned for the day. Families went for walks and children roller-skated on the empty Autobahn.

title: Udo Jürgens: “Griechischer Wein”
text: In 1974 Udo Jürgens sang “Griechischer Wein”, a song about Greek guest workers and their longing for home.

title: “Am laufenden Band”
text: From 1974 the Dutchman Rudi Carrell presented “Am laufenden Band”. At the end the winner had to remember the prizes passing by on a conveyor belt.

title: Jürgen Drews: “Ein Bett im Kornfeld”
text: In the summer of 1976 Jürgen Drews had his biggest hit with “Ein Bett im Kornfeld”.
listen: Jürgen Drews Ein Bett im Kornfeld

title: “Dschinghis Khan”
text: In 1979 the group Dschinghis Khan sang and danced the song of the same name at the Eurovision Song Contest in Jerusalem and came fourth.

title: Udo Lindenberg: “Sonderzug nach Pankow”
text: In 1983 Udo Lindenberg sang “Sonderzug nach Pankow”, cheekily asking Erich Honecker to let him perform in East Germany.

title: “Heimat”
text: In 1984 Edgar Reitz’s “Heimat” told the story of a village in the Hunsrück from 1919 on. Millions followed the Simon family week by week.

title: “Die Schwarzwaldklinik”
text: In October 1985 “Die Schwarzwaldklinik” began on ZDF. Professor Brinkmann’s hospital in the Black Forest drew some of the largest audiences in German television.

title: Steffi Graf’s Golden Slam
text: In 1988 Steffi Graf won all four Grand Slam tournaments and the Olympic gold medal in Seoul — a “Golden Slam”. She was 19.

title: World champions in Rome
text: On July 8, 1990, West Germany beat Argentina 1–0 in Rome to win the World Cup for the third time. Andreas Brehme scored the penalty.

title: Fausto Coppi, il Campionissimo
text: In 1952 Fausto Coppi won both the Giro d’Italia and the Tour de France in the same year, for the second time. Italy was divided between his fans and Bartali’s.

title: The Cortina Winter Olympics
text: In 1956 Cortina d’Ampezzo hosted the Winter Olympics, the first Games held in Italy and among the first to be shown on television.

title: The Moka on the stove
text: In the late 1950s the “little man with the moustache” advertised the Bialetti Moka Express on Carosello. Soon almost every kitchen had one bubbling on the stove.

title: “Divorce Italian Style”
text: In 1961 Marcello Mastroianni played a Sicilian baron with a plan in “Divorce Italian Style”. The comedy won an Oscar for its screenplay.

title: “Studio Uno”
text: From 1961 the Saturday-night show “Studio Uno” brought Mina and the Kessler twins into Italian living rooms.

title: Gino Paoli: “Sapore di sale”
text: In the summer of 1963 Gino Paoli sang “Sapore di sale”, the taste of salt on the skin after a day at the sea.

title: Bobby Solo: “Una lacrima sul viso”
text: At Sanremo in 1964 Bobby Solo sang “Una lacrima sul viso”. It did not win the festival, but it sold more than any other record that year.
listen: Bobby Solo Una lacrima sul viso

title: The Autostrada del Sole
text: On October 4, 1964, the Autostrada del Sole was completed, joining Milan and Naples. The drive between them became many hours shorter.

title: Jimmy Fontana: “Il mondo”
text: In 1965 Jimmy Fontana sang “Il mondo” — the world that never stops turning. It was a hit far beyond Italy.

title: “The Good, the Bad and the Ugly”
text: In 1966 Sergio Leone made “The Good, the Bad and the Ugly” with Clint Eastwood. Ennio Morricone’s music is recognised after two notes.
wiki: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly

title: Little Tony: “Cuore matto”
text: In 1967 Little Tony sang “Cuore matto” at Sanremo, and it stayed at the top of the charts for weeks.

title: Celentano: “Azzurro”
text: In 1968 Adriano Celentano recorded “Azzurro”, written by Paolo Conte. A long, too-blue summer afternoon became one of Italy’s best-loved songs.

title: Lucio Battisti
text: In 1969 Lucio Battisti sang “Acqua azzurra, acqua chiara” and “Mi ritorni in mente”. With the lyricist Mogol he wrote the songs a generation grew up with.
listen: Lucio Battisti Acqua azzurra acqua chiara

title: Mina: “Parole parole”
text: In 1972 Mina sang “Parole parole” with the actor Alberto Lupo, who whispered sweet nothings while she sang that they were only words.

title: The divorce referendum
text: On May 12, 1974, Italians voted on whether to keep the new divorce law. Nearly six in ten voted to keep it.

title: Rino Gaetano: “Gianna”
text: At Sanremo in 1978 Rino Gaetano came on stage in a top hat with a ukulele and sang “Gianna”.

title: Umberto Tozzi: “Gloria”
text: In 1979 Umberto Tozzi released “Gloria”, which was sung all over Europe that summer.

title: Mennea’s world record
text: On September 12, 1979, Pietro Mennea ran 200 metres in 19.72 seconds in Mexico City. The world record stood for almost 17 years.

title: Ricchi e Poveri: “Sarà perché ti amo”
text: At Sanremo in 1981 Ricchi e Poveri sang “Sarà perché ti amo”. It was one of the best-selling singles of the year.
listen: Ricchi e Poveri Sarà perché ti amo

title: Al Bano and Romina Power: “Felicità”
text: At Sanremo in 1982 Al Bano and Romina Power sang “Felicità” — happiness is a glass of wine and a sandwich.

title: Charles Trenet: “La Mer”
text: In 1946 Charles Trenet recorded “La Mer”. He said he had written it years earlier on a train, looking out at the Mediterranean.

title: Piaf: “La Vie en rose”
text: In 1947 Édith Piaf released “La Vie en rose”. It became her signature song and was soon sung around the world.
listen: Édith Piaf La Vie en rose

title: Abbé Pierre’s appeal
text: On February 1, 1954, in a bitterly cold winter, Abbé Pierre went on the radio to ask for help for the homeless. Blankets, stoves and money poured in from all over France.

title: Dalida: “Bambino”
text: In 1956 a young singer born in Cairo had her first great success with “Bambino”. Dalida stayed at the top for thirty years.

title: “Salut les copains”
text: From 1959 teenagers rushed home at five o’clock to hear “Salut les copains” on Europe 1. The radio show, and then the magazine, launched the yé-yé stars.

title: “Bonne nuit les petits”
text: From 1962, Nounours the bear came down from his cloud each evening to say goodnight to Nicolas and Pimprenelle — and to the children of France.

title: “Le Gendarme de Saint-Tropez”
text: In 1964 Louis de Funès put on the uniform of gendarme Cruchot in “Le Gendarme de Saint-Tropez”. Five more films followed.

title: “La Grande Vadrouille”
text: In 1966 Bourvil and Louis de Funès starred in “La Grande Vadrouille”. More than 17 million tickets were sold, a record in France for decades.

title: Polnareff: “La Poupée qui fait non”
text: In 1966 Michel Polnareff had his first hit with “La Poupée qui fait non”.
listen: Michel Polnareff La Poupée qui fait non

title: Dutronc: “Et moi, et moi, et moi”
text: In 1966 Jacques Dutronc sang “Et moi, et moi, et moi”, a wry song about thinking of oneself in a world of millions.
wiki: Et moi, et moi, et moi
listen: Jacques Dutronc Et moi et moi et moi

title: “Les Shadoks”
text: In 1968 the strange birds called the Shadoks arrived on television, pumping endlessly. France split into those who loved them and those who could not stand them.

title: Michel Fugain: “Une belle histoire”
text: In 1972 Michel Fugain and his Big Bazar sang “Une belle histoire”, about two strangers who meet on the holiday road.

title: Sardou: “La Maladie d’amour”
text: In 1973 Michel Sardou sang “La Maladie d’amour”, one of the great French hits of the decade.

title: “Apostrophes”
text: From January 1975, Bernard Pivot talked about books with their authors every Friday night on “Apostrophes”. Bookshops felt it the next morning.

title: Joe Dassin: “L’Été indien”
text: In 1975 Joe Dassin recorded “L’Été indien”, his biggest hit, remembering a season that exists only in North America.

title: Marie Myriam wins Eurovision
text: In 1977 Marie Myriam won the Eurovision Song Contest for France with “L’Oiseau et l’Enfant”.

title: “Les Bronzés”
text: In 1978 the Splendid troupe went on a holiday-club holiday in “Les Bronzés”. People still quote its lines.

title: The first Fête de la Musique
text: On June 21, 1982, France held its first Fête de la Musique. Everyone who could play was invited to go out and play in the street.

title: Yannick Noah wins Roland-Garros
text: On June 5, 1983, Yannick Noah won the French Open. He ran to embrace his father, who had jumped down onto the court.

title: Hinault’s fifth Tour
text: In 1985 Bernard Hinault, “the Badger”, won the Tour de France for the fifth time.

title: Basketball world champions
text: In 1950 Argentina hosted the first Basketball World Championship and won it, beating the United States in the final at Luna Park.

title: Atahualpa Yupanqui
text: With his guitar and songs like “Luna tucumana” and “El arriero”, Atahualpa Yupanqui carried the folk music of the Argentine countryside around the world.

title: “El Eternauta”
text: In 1957 the comic “El Eternauta” began to appear, in which a deadly snow falls on Buenos Aires. It became the most famous Argentine comic.

title: Los Chalchaleros
text: In the 1950s and 60s the four voices of Los Chalchaleros, from Salta, brought zambas into homes across the country.
listen: Los Chalchaleros Zamba de mi esperanza

title: The Cosquín festival
text: In January 1961 the town of Cosquín, in Córdoba, held its first national folk festival. “Aquí Cosquín!” has opened it every summer since.

title: The Torino
text: In 1966 the Torino went on sale, a car designed for and built in Argentina. In 1969 three Torinos surprised Europe in an 84-hour race at the Nürburgring.

title: “Hijitus”
text: In 1967 “Hijitus” came to television, the first Argentine cartoon series. With his magic hat he became Super Hijitus.

title: Lunches with Mirtha Legrand
text: In 1968 Mirtha Legrand began inviting guests to lunch on television. More than half a century later she was still at the table.

title: Leonardo Favio
text: In 1968 the film director Leonardo Favio turned singer, and “Fuiste mía un verano” was heard all over Latin America.
listen: Leonardo Favio Fuiste mía un verano

title: Almendra: “Muchacha (ojos de papel)”
text: In 1969 Luis Alberto Spinetta’s band Almendra recorded “Muchacha (ojos de papel)”, one of the best-loved songs of Argentine rock.

title: “Balada para un loco”
text: In 1969 Amelita Baltar sang “Balada para un loco”, by Astor Piazzolla and Horacio Ferrer. Some said it was not a tango at all; everyone sang it anyway.
listen: Amelita Baltar Balada para un loco

title: Carlos Monzón, world champion
text: On November 7, 1970, in Rome, Carlos Monzón knocked out Nino Benvenuti and became world middleweight champion. He defended the title 14 times.

title: “Rolando Rivas, taxista”
text: In 1972 the telenovela “Rolando Rivas, taxista” had the whole country watching the love story of a Buenos Aires taxi driver.

title: Piazzolla: “Libertango”
text: In 1974 Astor Piazzolla recorded “Libertango”, and his new tango was heard around the world.

title: León Gieco: “Sólo le pido a Dios”
text: In 1978 León Gieco wrote “Sólo le pido a Dios”, a prayer not to become indifferent to war and injustice. Mercedes Sosa made it known everywhere.
listen: León Gieco Sólo le pido a Dios

title: Serú Girán
text: Around 1980 Serú Girán, with Charly García, David Lebón, Pedro Aznar and Oscar Moro, were called “the Argentine Beatles”.

title: Los Abuelos de la Nada: “Mil horas”
text: In 1983, as democracy returned, Los Abuelos de la Nada released “Mil horas”, and everyone knew the chorus.
listen: Los Abuelos de la Nada Mil horas

title: Sabatini wins the US Open
text: In September 1990 Gabriela Sabatini beat Steffi Graf in New York to win the US Open.

title: Luiz Gonzaga: “Asa Branca”
text: In 1947 Luiz Gonzaga recorded “Asa Branca”, about leaving the dry Northeast and hoping to return. With his accordion, the “King of Baião” took the music of the sertão to the whole country.

title: “The oil is ours”
text: In 1953, after the campaign “O petróleo é nosso”, President Vargas created Petrobras.

title: Dorival Caymmi
text: In 1956 Dorival Caymmi sang “Maracangalha”. His songs about Bahia, the sea and the fishermen were known all over Brazil.

title: Maria Esther Bueno wins Wimbledon
text: In 1959 Maria Esther Bueno, from São Paulo, won Wimbledon at the age of 19. She won it twice more.

title: Celly Campello: “Estúpido Cupido”
text: In 1959 Celly Campello sang “Estúpido Cupido” and became the first star of Brazilian rock and roll.

title: Geraldo Vandré: “Caminhando”
text: At a song festival in 1968 Geraldo Vandré sang “Pra não dizer que não falei das flores”. It came second, the crowd sang along, and it became a hymn against the dictatorship.
wiki: Pra não dizer que não falei das flores
listen: Geraldo Vandré Pra não dizer que não falei das flores

title: “Jornal Nacional”
text: On September 1, 1969, TV Globo broadcast the first “Jornal Nacional”, the first news programme shown live across Brazil.

title: “País Tropical”
text: In 1969 Wilson Simonal sang Jorge Ben’s “País Tropical”: “I live in a tropical country, blessed by God and beautiful by nature.”

title: Roberto Carlos: “Detalhes”
text: In 1971 Roberto Carlos, “the King”, recorded “Detalhes”, one of the most loved of all his love songs.

title: “Águas de Março”
text: In 1972 Tom Jobim wrote “Águas de Março”. Two years later he recorded it as a duet with Elis Regina, laughing as they sang.
listen: Elis Regina Tom Jobim Águas de Março

title: Milton Nascimento and the Clube da Esquina
text: In 1972 Milton Nascimento, Lô Borges and their friends from Minas Gerais released the album “Clube da Esquina”.
listen: Milton Nascimento Clube da Esquina Nº 2

title: “Fantástico”
text: In August 1973 “Fantástico” began on TV Globo. Sunday night meant the weekend was nearly over.

title: Secos & Molhados
text: In 1973 Secos & Molhados appeared with painted faces and the high voice of Ney Matogrosso. Their first album sold in huge numbers.

title: Raul Seixas: “Gita”
text: In 1974 Raul Seixas released “Gita”, written with Paulo Coelho. “Toca Raul!” is still shouted at concerts.

title: João do Pulo’s world record
text: On October 15, 1975, at the Pan American Games in Mexico City, João Carlos de Oliveira jumped 17.89 metres in the triple jump, a world record.

title: Cartola: “As Rosas Não Falam”
text: In 1976 Cartola, one of the founders of the Mangueira samba school, recorded “As Rosas Não Falam”. He was in his late sixties.

title: “Sítio do Picapau Amarelo”
text: In 1977 Monteiro Lobato’s stories came to TV Globo. Children knew Emília the rag doll, Dona Benta and the Cuca.
wiki: Sítio do Picapau Amarelo (1977 TV series)

title: “Dancin’ Days”
text: In 1978 the telenovela “Dancin’ Days” brought the disco to Brazil — and striped lurex socks with high-heeled sandals.

title: Elis Regina: “O Bêbado e a Equilibrista”
text: In 1979 Elis Regina sang “O Bêbado e a Equilibrista”, which became the anthem of the amnesty and of the exiles coming home.
listen: Elis Regina O Bêbado e a Equilibrista

title: The 1982 team
text: On July 5, 1982, in Barcelona, the Brazil of Zico, Sócrates and Falcão lost 3–2 to Italy. Many still call it the best team that never won the World Cup.
wiki: Italy v Brazil (1982 FIFA World Cup)

title: “Roque Santeiro”
text: In 1985 almost the whole country stopped to watch “Roque Santeiro” and the widow Porcina, “who was a widow without ever having been one”.

title: Legião Urbana
text: In 1985 Legião Urbana, from Brasília, released their first album. Renato Russo’s songs spoke for a generation.

title: “Nosotros los pobres”
text: In 1948 Pedro Infante played the carpenter Pepe el Toro in “Nosotros los pobres”, one of the most-watched films in Mexican history.

title: Pedro Infante: “Amorcito corazón”
text: In the late 1940s Pedro Infante recorded “Amorcito corazón”, the bolero he sang and whistled on screen.

title: Cri-Cri, the singing cricket
text: On the radio station XEW, Francisco Gabilondo Soler sang as Cri-Cri, “el grillito cantor”. Generations of children grew up with his songs.

title: Pérez Prado and the mambo
text: Around 1950 the Cuban bandleader Dámaso Pérez Prado, working in Mexico City, set the whole world dancing the mambo.

title: “The Labyrinth of Solitude”
text: In 1950 Octavio Paz published “The Labyrinth of Solitude”, his essay on what it means to be Mexican. In 1990 he won the Nobel Prize in Literature.

title: “Cucurrucucú paloma”
text: In 1954 Tomás Méndez wrote “Cucurrucucú paloma”. Lola Beltrán, “Lola la Grande”, made it famous.

title: Joaquín Capilla’s gold
text: In 1956 the diver Joaquín Capilla won gold from the platform at the Melbourne Olympics, his fourth Olympic medal.

title: Los Teen Tops: “La plaga”
text: Around 1960 Los Teen Tops, with Enrique Guzmán, sang rock and roll in Spanish. “La plaga” was heard at every party.

title: “Macario”
text: In 1960 “Macario”, the story of a poor woodcutter who shares his turkey with Death, became the first Mexican film nominated for an Oscar.

title: Angélica María, “la novia de México”
text: In the early 1960s Angélica María sang, acted and smiled from every magazine cover. She was called “the sweetheart of Mexico”.

title: Javier Solís
text: In the 1960s Javier Solís, “the king of the bolero ranchero”, sang “Sombras” and “Payaso”. He died in 1966, aged only 34.

title: The Estadio Azteca opens
text: On May 29, 1966, the Estadio Azteca opened in Mexico City. It went on to host two World Cup finals.

title: Armando Manzanero
text: In 1967 Armando Manzanero, from Mérida, released “Adoro” and “Esta tarde vi llover”. His love songs were recorded all over the world.
listen: Armando Manzanero Esta tarde vi llover

title: “Siempre en Domingo”
text: From 1969 Raúl Velasco presented “Siempre en Domingo”. For almost thirty years, every singer who mattered appeared on his Sunday show.

title: José José: “El triste”
text: On March 15, 1970, a 22-year-old José José sang “El triste” at a song festival in Mexico City. He did not win, but the audience rose to its feet.

title: “El Chapulín Colorado”
text: In the early 1970s Chespirito put on a red suit with a yellow heart. “¡No contaban con mi astucia!” said El Chapulín Colorado.

title: Rigo Tovar
text: In the 1970s Rigo Tovar, from Matamoros, mixed cumbia with electric guitars and organ. Huge crowds came to hear him.

title: Daniel Bautista’s gold
text: In 1976 Daniel Bautista won the 20-kilometre walk at the Montreal Olympics, Mexico’s first Olympic gold medal in athletics.

title: A boy called Luis Miguel
text: In 1982 an eleven-year-old Luis Miguel released his first record. “El Sol de México” was just beginning.

title: Julio César Chávez
text: On September 13, 1984, Julio César Chávez, from Culiacán, won his first world title. He was unbeaten for the next nine years.

title: Bismillah Khan at the Red Fort
text: On August 15, 1947, Ustad Bismillah Khan played the shehnai at the Red Fort in Delhi as independent India’s flag was raised.

title: Hockey gold in London
text: In 1948, at the London Olympics, independent India’s hockey team beat Great Britain 4–0 in the final at Wembley.

title: Lata: “Aayega Aanewala”
text: In 1949 the song “Aayega Aanewala” from the film “Mahal” made a young Lata Mangeshkar famous. Listeners wrote to the radio asking who the singer was.

title: Vividh Bharati
text: In October 1957 All India Radio started Vividh Bharati. Film songs, requests from listeners and “Hawa Mahal” filled the evenings.

title: The Ambassador
text: From 1958 the Hindustan Ambassador was the car of ministers, taxi drivers and big families alike. It stayed in production for more than fifty years.

title: “Madhumati”
text: In 1958 Bimal Roy’s “Madhumati”, with Dilip Kumar and Vyjayanthimala, was the biggest hit of the year. People still sing “Suhana Safar”.

title: Milkha Singh in Rome
text: In 1960, at the Rome Olympics, Milkha Singh, “the Flying Sikh”, finished fourth in the 400 metres, missing a medal by a tenth of a second.

title: “Guide”
text: In 1965 Dev Anand and Waheeda Rehman starred in “Guide”, based on R. K. Narayan’s novel, with songs by S. D. Burman.

title: M. S. Subbulakshmi at the United Nations
text: In October 1966 M. S. Subbulakshmi sang at the United Nations in New York, carrying Carnatic music to the world.

title: The Amul girl
text: In 1966 a little girl in a polka-dotted dress began appearing on Amul butter hoardings, with a new joke about the news every week. “Utterly butterly delicious.”

title: Ravi Shankar at Monterey
text: In June 1967 Ravi Shankar played the sitar for a whole afternoon at the Monterey Pop Festival in California.

title: Gavaskar’s first series
text: In 1971 a 21-year-old Sunil Gavaskar scored 774 runs in his first Test series, and India won in the West Indies for the first time.

title: Asha Bhosle: “Dum Maro Dum”
text: In 1971 Asha Bhosle sang R. D. Burman’s “Dum Maro Dum” in the film “Hare Rama Hare Krishna”. It was the sound of a new decade.

title: “Anand”
text: In 1971 Rajesh Khanna played a dying man who teaches everyone around him to live, in Hrishikesh Mukherjee’s “Anand”.

title: “Pakeezah”
text: In 1972 “Pakeezah”, which had taken Kamal Amrohi some fourteen years to finish, was released. Meena Kumari died a few weeks later.

title: The Bajaj Chetak
text: From 1972 the Bajaj Chetak scooter carried whole families. In some years people waited a very long time for theirs to be delivered.

title: “Zanjeer”
text: In 1973 “Zanjeer” made Amitabh Bachchan a star. The “angry young man” had arrived.

title: Prakash Padukone wins the All England
text: In March 1980 Prakash Padukone became the first Indian to win the All England badminton championship.

title: Nazia Hassan: “Aap Jaisa Koi”
text: In 1980 fifteen-year-old Nazia Hassan sang “Aap Jaisa Koi” for the film “Qurbani”, and disco came to Hindi film music.

title: The Maruti 800
text: On December 14, 1983, Indira Gandhi handed over the keys of the first Maruti 800. A small car of one’s own was suddenly within reach.

title: “Hum Log”
text: In 1984 “Hum Log” began on Doordarshan, India’s first television serial. At the end of each episode Ashok Kumar came on to talk it over.

title: P. T. Usha in Los Angeles
text: In 1984, at the Los Angeles Olympics, P. T. Usha missed the bronze medal in the 400 metres hurdles by one hundredth of a second.

title: “Mile Sur Mera Tumhara”
text: On Independence Day 1988, Doordarshan first showed “Mile Sur Mera Tumhara”, sung in many of India’s languages by its best-loved voices.

title: “Mahabharat”
text: From October 1988, B. R. Chopra’s “Mahabharat” was shown on Sunday mornings. Streets fell quiet while it was on.

title: Pacho Galán: “Ay cosita linda”
text: In 1955 Pacho Galán, from Soledad, recorded “Ay cosita linda” in a new rhythm he called merecumbé. It was soon played all over Latin America.

title: Los Corraleros de Majagual
text: In the 1960s Los Corraleros de Majagual brought together accordions, brass and singers like Alfredo Gutiérrez and Calixto Ochoa. No December party was complete without them.
listen: Los Corraleros de Majagual Festival en Guararé

title: José Barros: “La Piragua”
text: In 1969 José Barros, from El Banco, wrote the cumbia “La Piragua”, about Guillermo Cubillos’s big canoe on the Magdalena river.

title: Claudia de Colombia
text: In the 1970s Claudia de Colombia was the voice of the romantic ballad, heard on radios all over the country.
listen: Claudia de Colombia Nuestra historia de amor

title: El Binomio de Oro
text: From 1976 Rafael Orozco’s voice and Israel Romero’s accordion made the Binomio de Oro the most popular vallenato group in the country.
listen: Binomio de Oro Rafael Orozco La creciente

title: Amber Gurung: “Nau Lakh Tara”
text: In the early 1960s Amber Gurung composed and sang “Nau Lakh Tara”, about Nepalis living far from home. Years later he wrote the music for Nepal’s national anthem.

title: Prem Dhoj Pradhan
text: From the 1960s the soft voice of Prem Dhoj Pradhan was heard on Radio Nepal in romantic songs that are still loved.

title: Gopal Yonjan
text: In the 1970s Gopal Yonjan wrote many of the songs Narayan Gopal sang. The two were “mit”, sworn friends.

title: Kumar Basnet’s folk songs
text: From the 1960s Kumar Basnet walked through the hills collecting folk songs and sang them on Radio Nepal.

title: “May There Always Be Sunshine”
text: In 1962 the children’s song “May There Always Be Sunshine” was written. The next year Tamara Miansarova won the Sopot song festival with it.
listen: Тамара Миансарова Пусть всегда будет солнце

title: Muslim Magomayev
text: In the 1960s the baritone Muslim Magomayev, from Baku, could sing both opera and pop songs. His concerts filled stadiums.

title: “The Bremen Town Musicians”
text: In 1969 the cartoon musical “The Bremen Town Musicians” came out. Its songs were on records in almost every home with children.
listen: Бременские музыканты Ничего на свете лучше нету

title: Sofia Rotaru: “Chervona Ruta”
text: In 1971 Sofia Rotaru sang “Chervona Ruta”, written by the young Ukrainian composer Volodymyr Ivasyuk.

title: Samotsvety: “My Address Is the Soviet Union”
text: In 1972 the group Samotsvety sang “My address is not a house or a street, my address is the Soviet Union”.

title: Anna German: “Nadezhda”
text: In 1974 the Polish singer Anna German recorded “Nadezhda” (“Hope”). Cosmonauts were said to listen to it before every flight.

title: “Den Pobedy”
text: In 1975, thirty years after the war ended, Lev Leshchenko sang “Den Pobedy” (“Victory Day”). It has been sung every May 9 since.

title: Yuri Antonov
text: In the early 1980s Yuri Antonov’s songs, like “Under the Roof of Your House”, were played from every open window.

title: Zemlyane: “Grass by the Home”
text: In 1983 the group Zemlyane sang “Grass by the Home”, about a cosmonaut who dreams of the green grass of Earth.
